items.question: Per Sect. 3.1.2, what is the correct interpretation of an amber 'Caution' alert on the master list?
options: A condition requiring immediate crew awareness and possibly subsequent (not immediate) crew response
A condition requiring immediate crew awareness and immediate crew response
A condition requiring crew awareness only, with no crew response required
Normal operation of a crew-selected function
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.2: Warning (red) requires immediate crew awareness and immediate response; Caution (amber) requires immediate awareness and possibly subsequent (not immediate) response; Advisory (white) requires awareness/monitoring with no response required.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.1.5, what does the urgency term 'LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE' mean?
options: Land without delay at the nearest adequate site at which a safe approach and landing can be made
Continue the flight as planned, with intermediate landings permitted
Landing site and duration of flight are at the pilot's discretion
Landing in water or trees should be considered only as a last resort, primary consideration is occupant survival
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.5: LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE means land without delay at the nearest adequate site (open field) where a safe approach and landing can be made. The last option describes LAND IMMEDIATELY instead.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.1.6 (Cabin emergency evacuation), what is the first step in the procedure?
options: Lift the door handle, then slide the sliding door aft to open
Immediately pull the window curtain handle to remove it
Pull the red or yellow/black handle/strap to remove the seal
Push forcefully at the red/white or yellow/black circle markings on the window
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.6: the cabin emergency evacuation procedure starts with lifting the door handle and sliding the door aft to open; if the sliding door is jammed, the crew proceeds to removing the window curtain, cap, and seal, then pushes out the window at the marked circles to exit.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.1.7, how many in-flight resets should crew members limit themselves to for a given tripped circuit breaker?
options: One in-flight reset; no attempt should be made if it trips a second time
Two in-flight resets are permitted before landing
Unlimited resets, provided the aircraft logbook is updated
Zero — in-flight resets are never permitted under any circumstances
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.7: crew members should limit resetting of a cb to one in-flight reset where required; no attempt should be made to reset it if it trips a second time.

items.question: Both autopilot systems are lost (AP on Warning Unit, AUTOPILOT on ML, voice 'HANDS ON'). Per Sect. 3.2.1, if re-engaging AP1+AP2 is unsuccessful, what is the correct next step?
options: Reduce airspeed to VNE AP OFF (110 kt), then LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE
Increase airspeed to VNE AEO and continue flight
Immediately perform an autorotation landing
Switch BKUP sw ON and continue flight without further restriction
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.1: fly manually and try to re-engage AP2+AP1; if unsuccessful, reduce airspeed to VNE AP OFF (110 kt) and LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per the AP ACTUATOR caution note in Sect. 3.2.2, if the collective SEMA has failed, how must the autopilot be operated?
options: Only in 3-axis mode, with the collective axis controlled manually
Fully in 4-axis mode with no restriction
The autopilot must be switched off entirely
Only the backup SAS may be used, AP1/AP2 are inoperative
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.2 note: if the collective SEMA has failed, the autopilot can only be operated in 3-axis mode and the collective axis must be controlled manually.

items.question: For the AP TRIM OFF caution, per Sect. 3.2.2, what determines whether the crew continues the flight or must LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE after AP2 recycling is unsuccessful?
options: Whether the flight is VFR/DPIFR (continue, attentive hands-on) versus SPIFR (land as soon as practicable, attentive hands-on)
Whether the aircraft is above or below 5000 ft PA
Whether the mast moment is in the amber or red range
Whether both engines are operating normally
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.2 AP TRIM OFF procedure: if VFR or DPIFR (IMC), continue flight (fly attentive hands-on); if SPIFR (IMC), LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE (fly attentive hands-on).

items.question: Per Sect. 3.2.3.1 (Stuck beep trim), what caution applies AFTER LANDING if the runaway continued and the aircraft had to land with high control forces?
options: Flying controls hands-on and feet-on until the main rotor has stopped
The parking brake must remain engaged for 30 minutes
Both engines must be shut down using the emergency shutdown procedure
The affected trim actuator must be reset before the next flight without exception
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.1 caution: after landing, flying controls hands-on and feet-on until the main rotor has stopped, since high control forces on the affected axis may persist.

items.question: The 'Autopilot fly-up' condition (Sect. 3.2.3.4) is triggered under which circumstance?
options: The autopilot is in CH.RT or HEIGHT mode and the aircraft descends unexpectedly
The autopilot disengages due to a NAV frequency change
Both AHRS units fail simultaneously
The collective lever position sensor fails
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.4: FLY-UP is triggered when the autopilot is in CH.RT or HEIGHT mode and the aircraft descends unexpectedly; the FND AFCS strip replaces the mode label with >FLY-UP<.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.2.3.7, what happens to AFCS operation when the collective lever position sensor fails?
options: AFCS operation degrades to 3-axis operation, and COLL LINK - DEG appears on the FLI
The autopilot disengages completely with no reconfiguration possible
Only the yaw axis is affected; pitch and roll remain fully coupled
The backup SAS automatically engages and AP1/AP2 are locked out
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.7: collective lever position sensor failure shows COLL LINK - DEG on the FLI; AFCS operation degrades to 3-axis operation, and transient pitch, yaw, roll deviations may occur after collective movement.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.2.3.14, 'Upper mode override' occurs when the AFCS detects the pilot's hands/feet on the controls overriding the selected upper mode. Which upper mode is the sole exception where no OVERRIDE indication is shown?
options: HOVER mode
GTC mode
HEIGHT mode
CR.HT mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.14: the AFCS strip shows OVERRIDE alternating indication for any upper mode being overridden, except GTC mode, for which no OVERRIDE indication is shown.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.1.3, the MM EXCEEDED warning (mast moment) is triggered by which accumulated condition on the H145 D3?
options: >83% for more than 60 seconds, or >90% for more than 20 seconds, or >95%
>90% for more than 15 seconds, or >95% for more than 5 seconds, or >100% (H145 D2 thresholds)
Any single momentary spike above 54%
Sustained value above 68% for more than 60 seconds
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.1.3: on the H145 D3, MM EXCEEDED (warning) triggers at >83% for more than 60 sec, >90% for more than 20 sec, or >95%. These accumulated thresholds are higher than the H145 D2's (>90%/15s, >95%/5s, >100%), reflecting the 5-bladed rotor's different mast moment dynamics.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.2, AIR1 DATA FAIL AIR2 (both ADCs failed) requires which crew response?
options: Verify altitude and airspeed on FND/IESI, then LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE
Continue flight with no further action, both ADCs are non-essential
Immediately perform a double engine emergency shutdown
Disengage the backup SAS and fly manually for the remainder of the flight
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.2: with both ADC1 and ADC2 failed, IESI air data is shown on all MFDs, NR may increase to 104%, IAS upper modes decouple, and vertical speed indication disappears; the crew shall verify FND/IESI indications and LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.2, on the ground with an AMC1/2 FAIL (complete channel A+B loss) caution, what must the crew do if the engines are already started?
options: Perform a double engine shutdown
Continue with a normal takeoff, the condition is advisory only
Start engines individually one at a time to isolate the fault
Only shut down the affected engine, leave the other running
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.2: for AMC1 FAIL or AMC2 FAIL on ground — do not start engines; if engines are already started, perform a double engine shutdown. In flight, LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.2, ATT1 FAIL ATT2 (both AHRS units failed), what remains as a reliable attitude source and what is the required crew action?
options: IESI remains a reliable ATT source; LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, flying attentive hands-on
The standby compass becomes the sole attitude reference; continue flight normally
GPS-derived attitude data automatically substitutes; no crew action required
There is no reliable backup; the crew must autorotate immediately
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.2: with both AHRS failed, IESI remains as the reliable ATT source; the compass rose and V/S indicate amber; the crew shall LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, flying attentive hands-on.

items.question: Per the radar altimeter failure procedure (Sect. 3.3.3.5), which capability is explicitly stated as inoperative, requiring the pilot to use decision altitude instead?
options: Decision height
HTAWS mode 1 only
VORTEX warning (fully reliable, unaffected)
ILS glideslope capture
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.3.5 warning: decision height is inoperative — use decision altitude when possible. The autopilot will also not perform automatic level-off.

items.question: Per the radar altimeter failure procedure (Sect. 3.3.3.5), what minimum height must be maintained over water (except for takeoff and landing)?
options: 500 ft
200 ft
50 ft
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.3.5: with the radar altimeter failed, maintain at least 500 ft over water, except for takeoff and landing, and disengage the AFCS CR.HT mode.

items.question: Per the V NE indication failure procedure (CHECK VNE, Sect. 3.3.3.8), what is V NE one engine inoperative (V NE OEI) set to?
options: 110 kt or V NE AEO, whichever is less
150 kt fixed, regardless of AEO value
90 kt or V NE AEO, whichever is less
130 kt fixed, regardless of AEO value
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.3.8: when V NE cannot be computed automatically, V NE OEI is determined as 110 kt or V NE AEO (from the applicable table), whichever is less; V NE power off is 90 kt or V NE AEO, whichever is less.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.4, when DATABASE EXPIRED is displayed and the planned flight requires mission functions (HTAWS, DMAP, SVS), what is the required action?
options: Perform a double engine shutdown
Continue flight without restriction
Only disable the affected mission function and continue
Divert immediately regardless of flight phase
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.4 DATABASE EXPIRED: if the flight requires use of mission functions relying on the expired database (HTAWS, DMAP, SVS), perform a double engine shutdown; otherwise, continue flight.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.4, HDG1 MAG HDG FAIL HDG2 (both magnetometers failed) requires which crew action?
options: Use the standby compass as the leading source, then LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE
Continue flight normally with no change, as GPS heading fully substitutes
Immediately switch to backup SAS and disengage all autopilot modes
Land immediately at the nearest airport, regardless of terrain
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.4: with both magnetometers failed, use the standby compass as the leading source (cross-check digital map heading references against it), and LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.4.1, the AVIONICS OVHT caution indicates the avionics compartment temperature has exceeded what threshold?
options: 55°C (or 65°C, depending on installed equipment)
40°C fixed
70°C fixed
100°C fixed
items.explanation: Sect. 3.4.1: AVIONICS OVHT indicates upper and/or lower avionics compartment overheat, exceeding 55°C (or 65°C depending on installed equipment). If the caution remains after maximum ventilation is set, LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.4.1, the HEATING OVERTEMP caution is triggered when the mixing valve outlet temperature exceeds what value?
items.explanation: Sect. 3.4.1: HEATING OVERTEMP triggers when mixing valve inlet temperature exceeds 82°C, or mixing valve outlet temperature exceeds 105°C; it extinguishes once inlet temperature drops below 71°C.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.5.1.1, in an intercom failure affecting BOTH the pilot's and copilot's systems, which VHF radio does each crew member fall back to in BACKUP mode?
options: Pilot uses VHF2, copilot uses VHF1
Pilot uses VHF1, copilot uses VHF2
Both use VHF1 simultaneously
Both revert to the standby guard frequency only
items.explanation: Sect. 3.5.1.1: if both intercom systems are affected, select BACKUP on any ACU's EMER switch — the pilot can then receive/transmit on VHF2, and the copilot on VHF1.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.5.3.4, a stuck VHF COM transmit key automatically stops transmission after how long?
options: 30 seconds
10 seconds
60 seconds
5 seconds
items.explanation: Sect. 3.5.3.4: the REMOTE KEY STUCK message indicates the com push-to-talk key is stuck; transmission automatically stops after 30 seconds.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.5.4.2, if a glideslope and/or localizer discrepancy occurs during final approach and the erroneous source cannot be determined, what should the crew do?
options: Use an alternate approach procedure that does not require the erroneous source, to complete the flight
Continue the approach on the same source and monitor closely
Immediately declare an emergency and divert to the nearest suitable airport
Disengage all AFCS modes and complete the approach fully manually on the same approach
items.explanation: Sect. 3.5.4.2: push GA, perform a missed approach; if the erroneous source can be determined, deselect it and repeat using a single source; if it cannot be determined, use an alternate approach procedure not requiring the erroneous source.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.6.1, if the DOOR OPEN caution remains on and door status cannot be confirmed by visual inspection, what is the required action?
options: LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE
Continue flight and ignore the caution
LAND IMMEDIATELY regardless of terrain
Reduce airspeed to VNE - 20kt only, no landing required
items.explanation: Sect. 3.6.1: close the doors and check they are latched; if visual inspection confirms all doors properly latched, continue flight; if the caution remains and door status is uncertain, LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.7.5 (Electrical Master Boxes installed, S/N 20070 and S/N 21016 and subsequent), the BAT OVERHEAT warning indicates battery temperature has exceeded what threshold?
items.explanation: Sect. 3.7.5: BAT OVERHEAT indicates battery overtemperature above 70°C. In flight, BAT MSTR sw OFF and LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE; the battery must be inspected or replaced prior to the next flight.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.7.6 (Electrical Master Boxes installed), with both generators disconnected (GEN1 DISCONNECTED GEN2) and EMER SHD BUS switched ON, what is the resulting flight time limitation?
options: Flight time is reduced to less than 30 minutes
No flight time restriction applies
Flight time is limited to 2 hours
Flight time is limited to 10 minutes
items.explanation: Sect. 3.7.6 warning: if EMER SHD BUS sw is ON (both generators failed, battery-only power), flight time is reduced to less than 30 minutes; the crew must land within 30 minutes to avoid total electrical failure.

items.question: In case of total electrical failure, per the warning in Sect. 3.7.6, approximately how long will IESI continue to provide airspeed, altitude, and attitude data?
options: Approximately 30 minutes
Approximately 5 minutes
Approximately 2 hours
Indefinitely, IESI is unaffected
items.explanation: Sect. 3.7.6 warning: in case of total electrical failure, IESI will provide airspeed, altitude, and attitude data for approximately 30 minutes; all COM/NAV, MFD indications, and aircraft stabilization will be lost.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.7.6, GEN1 OVERHEAT (or GEN2 OVERHEAT) requires a single engine emergency shutdown if the caution remains on for how long after switching the affected generator off?
options: More than 1 minute
More than 5 minutes
More than 10 seconds
The shutdown is never required for a generator overheat
items.explanation: Sect. 3.7.6: for GEN1/2 OVERHEAT, switch the affected GEN off and reduce electrical load; if the caution remains on for more than 1 minute, establish OEI conditions, identify the affected engine, and perform a single engine emergency shutdown, then LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: In HIGE (hover in ground effect), per Sect. 3.8.1 (ENG1 and 2 FAIL, double engine failure), what is the correct procedure?
options: Apply right pedal to stop yaw, establish landing attitude, raise collective to cushion landing
Immediately enter autorotation glide at Vy
Apply left pedal to stop yaw and lower collective fully
Increase collective immediately to maintain altitude
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.1: for a double engine failure in HIGE, apply right pedal as necessary to stop yaw, establish landing attitude, and raise the collective lever to cushion the landing. In flight, perform autorotation instead.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.2 (ENG CHIP caution), what are the two IN-FLIGHT alternatives after establishing OEI flight condition and identifying the affected engine?
options: Perform a single engine emergency shutdown, OR set ENG MAIN sw to IDLE and closely monitor the affected engine to keep it available for landing
Perform a double engine emergency shutdown in all cases
Continue flight with no further action required, chip detection is advisory only
Immediately activate FADEC EMER mode on both engines
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2: after establishing OEI condition and identifying the affected engine, alternative 1 is a single engine emergency shutdown; alternative 2 is setting the affected ENG MAIN sw to IDLE, closely monitoring parameters, so the engine remains available for landing if needed.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.2, if BOTH engines show ENG1/2 FUEL FILTER caution simultaneously, what is the required urgency of landing?
options: LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE, be prepared for double engine failure
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, be prepared for single engine failure
Continue flight, this indication requires no landing
LAND IMMEDIATELY, regardless of terrain
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2: a single ENGi FUEL FILTER caution requires LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE (be prepared for single engine failure); if both caution indications appear, LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE and be prepared for double engine failure.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.2 (ENG1/2 OVERSPEED), when one engine has been shut down automatically by its overspeed protection system, what happens to the other engine's overspeed protection?
options: It becomes interlocked to an inactive status, so the normal engine is no longer protected against overspeed
It automatically doubles its sensitivity to compensate
Nothing changes; both systems remain fully independent
It automatically transfers protection duties to the FADEC EMER mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2 caution: when an engine has been shut down by its overspeed protection system, the other engine's overspeed protection system is interlocked to an inactive status, so the normal engine is no longer protected against power turbine overspeed.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.4.2 (Autorotation), what is the minimum rate-of-descent airspeed?
options: 60 KIAS
90 KIAS
45 KIAS
75 KIAS
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.2: maximum range airspeed in autorotation is 90 KIAS; minimum rate-of-descent airspeed is 60 KIAS. Normal procedure targets Vy.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.4.2 (Autorotation), at approximately what height AGL should the flare attitude of 15° to 20° first be established?
options: 100 ft AGL
500 ft AGL
50 ft AGL
8-12 ft AGL
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.2: at approximately 100 ft AGL, establish flare attitude (approx. 15° to 20°) to reduce forward speed and rate of descent; at approximately 8-12 ft AGL, reduce flare attitude to approximately 10° and raise collective to cushion the landing.

items.question: Per the warning preceding Sect. 3.8.4.3 (Single engine emergency shutdown), what must the pilot do before shutting down an engine in flight?
options: Double-check via the master list which engine is affected, using additional VMS indications (e.g. N1 below 60%) to confirm; in case of doubt, do not shut it down until after landing
Immediately shut down whichever engine the pilot first suspects, without further verification
Always shut down engine 1 first, regardless of which engine is actually affected
Wait until both engines show failure indications before shutting either down
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.3 warning: prior to performing engine emergency shutdown in flight, the pilot shall double-check that the affected engine will be shut down, using the master list and additional VMS indications; in case of doubt, do not perform a single engine emergency shutdown until after landing.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.4.4 (Inflight restart), when is an inflight restart explicitly NOT to be attempted?
options: If the cause of engine failure is obviously mechanical
If the flameout occurred above 5000 ft PA
If FADEC DEGRADED was active before the failure
Inflight restart is never permitted under any circumstances
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.4 caution: do not attempt an inflight restart if the cause of engine failure is obviously mechanical.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.8.4.5 (Single engine landing), what airspeed and maximum rate of descent apply on final approach at 50 ft AGL?
options: 30 KIAS, max 500 ft/min rate of descent
60 KIAS, max 1000 ft/min rate of descent
90 KIAS, max 200 ft/min rate of descent
20 KIAS, max 1500 ft/min rate of descent
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.5: on final at 50 ft AGL, reduce airspeed to 30 KIAS with a maximum rate of descent of 500 ft/min, then reduce airspeed further at touchdown and raise the collective to cushion the landing.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.9.1 (Engine fire), the fire extinguisher bottle begins discharging automatically only once which condition is met?
options: N1 of the affected engine is 45% or below
N2 has dropped to zero
The aircraft is fully on the ground
TOT has dropped below 400°C
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.1 note: after BOT 1/BOT 2 pb is pressed, the extinguisher bottle will begin discharging when N1 ≤ 45%. After discharge, the BOT 1 label and EXT light go off and BOT 2 label comes on.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.9.1 (Engine fire, in flight), if the FIRE warning remains on even after both extinguisher bottles have been discharged, what is the required urgency of landing?
options: LAND IMMEDIATELY
LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE
CONTINUE FLIGHT to the nearest suitable airfield
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.1: if the FIRE warning disappears after using the extinguisher bottles, LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE; if it is still on after 1 minute, discharge the second bottle; if the FIRE warning still remains on, LAND IMMEDIATELY.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.9.3.2, in an in-flight electrical fire/short circuit where the source cannot be positively identified, what should the crew be prepared for per the warning?
options: Loss of all electrical systems and indications, except IESI
A momentary radio blackout of less than 10 seconds only
Complete loss of hydraulic pressure
Automatic activation of the fire extinguisher bottles
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.3.2 warning: be prepared for loss of all electrical systems and indications, except IESI, when the source of an electrical fire cannot be positively identified and both bus ties/generators must be switched off.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.10.1, when BOTH LOW FUEL warning lights are illuminated, what is the required action?
options: LAND WITHIN 8 MINUTES
LAND WITHIN 30 MINUTES
Expect a single engine failure only, no landing time limit
Continue flight, monitor fuel quantity only
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.1: if both LOW FUEL warning lights are on, LAND WITHIN 8 MINUTES — after 8 minutes, a flameout of both engines must be expected. If only one light is on, expect a single engine failure after approximately 10 minutes.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.10.1, the LOW FUEL warning is triggered when the respective supply tank fuel quantity drops below what value?
options: 26 kg
50 kg
10 kg
40 kg
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.1: FUEL1/2 LOW warning triggers when the respective supply tank fuel quantity is below 26 kg; endurance indication is no longer shown.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.10.2, if BOTH the aft and forward fuel transfer pumps have failed (AFT+FWD FUEL PMP) and FUEL RESERVE subsequently appears, what is the required action?
options: LAND WITHIN 20 MINUTES
LAND WITHIN 8 MINUTES
Continue flight, no landing time restriction applies
LAND WITHIN 60 MINUTES
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.2: with both AFT and FWD fuel pumps failed, if FUEL RESERVE subsequently appears, LAND WITHIN 20 MIN.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.10.2 (FUEL QTY FAIL caution), what critical safety function remains fully operational and independent of the fuel quantity indication system?
options: The LOW FUEL warning and 'FUEL LOW' voice message
The aircraft weight calculation
The VNE computation
The FUEL RESERVE caution
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.2 caution: the LOW FUEL warning and 'FUEL LOW' voice message remain fully operational and are independent of the fuel quantity indication system, even though part of that system has failed.

items.question: A tail rotor drive failure in hover is indicated by which yawing motion, per Sect. 3.11.1.1?
options: Severe yawing motion nose right
Severe yawing motion nose left
No yawing motion, only a loss of altitude
Oscillating yaw, alternating left and right
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.1.1: tail rotor failure in power-on flight is indicated by a severe yawing motion nose right (complete loss of tail rotor thrust). In HIGE, lower the collective immediately and establish landing attitude.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.11.1.2 (Tail rotor drive/fixed-pitch tail rotor control failure, forward flight), what minimum airspeed should be maintained?
options: 70 KIAS or higher
40 KIAS or higher
100 KIAS or higher
50 KIAS or higher
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.1.2: adjust the collective to obtain minimum sideslip angle, and maintain 70 KIAS or higher; a hard, flat landing surface and left crosswind are advantageous.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.11.2 (MGB LOW PRESS warning, in flight), what is the maximum time before landing, and what airspeed should be flown?
options: LAND IMMEDIATELY, maximum 15 minutes, at VY with reduced power
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, no time limit, normal cruise speed
LAND WITHIN 30 minutes at maximum continuous power
Continue flight, MGB LOW PRESS requires no landing
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.2: with MGB LOW PRESS in flight, reduce power, set airspeed to VY, and LAND IMMEDIATELY (maximum 15 minutes) — MGB loss-of-oil capability has been demonstrated on a bench test at VY power setting for 30 minutes.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.11.3 (ROTOR BRAKE caution), what happens if the rotor brake is engaged during an attempted engine start?
options: The engines will not start with the rotor brake engaged
The engines start normally, but at reduced power
Only engine 1 is inhibited from starting
There is no interlock; engines start normally
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.3 note: engines will not start with the rotor brake engaged. If the ROTOR BRAKE caution remains on after checking the lever fully down, LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.

items.question: Per the warning in Sect. 3.12.1, what action involving the hydraulic test switch is explicitly prohibited in flight?
options: Operating the TEST HYD switch in flight
Selecting the VMS page during a HYD caution
Reducing airspeed below VY during a hydraulic caution
Using the collective friction lock
items.explanation: Sect. 3.12.1 warning: do not operate the TEST HYD switch in flight. For HYD1/2 LOW PRESS, LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.12.1 (HYD1 TR SHUT OFF caution), what caution applies if this occurs in combination with a failure of hydraulic system 2?
options: Fenestron actuation will be lost
The main rotor will lose all hydraulic boost
Only the collective axis is affected
No further caution applies; system 2 always compensates fully
items.explanation: Sect. 3.12.1 caution: HYD1 TR SHUT OFF indicates the tail rotor (Fenestron) hydraulic shut-off valve for system 1 has activated; in combination with a failure of hydraulic system 2, Fenestron actuation will be lost.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.13 (LAVCS FAIL), the active vibration control system may automatically shut down due to excessive vibrations above what threshold?
items.explanation: Sect. 3.13: LAVCS FAIL can result from no power on the non-essential bus, the LAVCS switch being OFF, a built-in test failure on ground, or automatic shutdown due to excessive vibrations exceeding 0.5 g.

items.question: Per Sect. 3.3.2, the MM SERVICE NEEDED caution (mast moment) on the H145 D3 is triggered when accumulated mast moment surpasses which lowest threshold?
options: >75% for more than 90 seconds
>66% for more than 60 seconds (H145 D2 threshold)
>54% for more than 30 seconds
>95% for more than 5 seconds
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.2: on the H145 D3, MM SERVICE NEEDED (caution) triggers at >75% for more than 90 seconds, >83% for 30-60 sec, or >90% for up to 20 sec — all higher than the H145 D2's 66%/79% thresholds, reflecting the 5-bladed rotor's mast moment characteristics.
